title: Make a Moon Phases Calendar and Calculator
desc: The child prints, cuts and assembles a paper wheel (with a brass fastener) that shows the Moon's phase for each day, roughly when it rises and sets, and where to look for it.
how: Build it at the start of a month and check the real Moon against the wheel each evening; it is set for the northern hemisphere, which suits India.

title: Oreo Moon Phases
desc: Printable activity in which the child opens sandwich cookies and scrapes off the cream filling to model the main phases of the Moon.
how: Any cream biscuit works; arrange the finished 'phases' in a circle around a ball for Earth with a torch as the Sun.

title: Moon Phases with Cookies
desc: Lesson in which children make Moon phases from cookies, arrange them in a circle, put an object for Earth in the middle and a Sun outside to see where the light comes from.
how: Use after the Oreo Moon activity to talk about why the lit part of the Moon changes.

title: NASA Space Place Games
desc: Collection of free browser games about space and Earth, including Solar System Switch-a-Roo (combine clues to find planets and moons), Helios (how the Sun makes energy) and a Mars rover coding game.
how: Let the child pick one game per session after a solar-system lesson.

title: NASA Space Place: Things to Make and Do
desc: Menu of hands-on space and Earth science projects that children can make at home with simple materials.
how: Browse together and choose a project that matches the week's topic.

title: PDFs of Space Place Activities
desc: List of printable PDF versions of Space Place hands-on activities, such as the Oreo Moon phases activity.
how: Print a few in advance for screen-free science time.

title: Helios: A Game About How the Sun Makes Energy
desc: Timed matching puzzle where the child swaps and drags particles to join hydrogen into helium, the way the Sun releases energy; the score counts completed reactions.
how: Best for older children after learning that the Sun is a star that gives us light and heat.

title: Space Volcano Explorer
desc: Interactive map of the solar system where the child clicks marked places to explore volcanoes on Earth, Venus and other worlds, and learns about active, dormant and extinct volcanoes.
how: Use alongside a lesson on volcanoes to show they are not only found on Earth.

title: Real World: Planetary Volcanoes (video)
desc: Short NASA video about volcanoes on Earth and on other planets and moons in the solar system.

title: Pocket Solar System (facilitator guide)
desc: The child folds a long strip of receipt paper to place the Sun, planets and asteroids at scaled distances, and sees how much empty space lies between planets.
how: A till roll or strips of paper taped together about the child's height work well.

title: Solar Clock Activity
desc: Using a printable template, the child builds a sundial that tells time from the Sun's position and then checks it against a watch.
how: Needs a sunny day; take readings every hour to see the shadow move.

title: Create a Sundial
desc: The child cuts out a printable template, fixes it with clay or dough and glue, and uses it outdoors on a sunny day while learning how people told time by the Sun.

title: Why Does Earth Have Seasons?
desc: Illustrated explainer showing that seasons come from the tilt of Earth's axis, not its distance from the Sun, and why northern winter happens when Earth is closest to the Sun.
how: Read together, then act it out by walking a tilted ball around a lamp.

title: Why Do We Have Seasons? (lesson)
desc: Teacher-written lesson in which children use a model to see how Earth's tilted axis causes different seasons through the year in the northern and southern hemispheres.

title: Climate Kids: Water
desc: Section of short illustrated articles on where Earth's water is found, from oceans and rivers to clouds, including 'What Is the Water Cycle?'.

title: Make a Zine: The Water Cycle
desc: The child folds and fills in a small paper booklet covering the water cycle's stages: precipitation, runoff, infiltration, evapotranspiration and condensation.

title: How Do Clouds Form?
desc: Short readable 'wonder' explaining how invisible water vapour cools as air rises and condenses into tiny droplets on dust and salt 'cloud seeds'.
how: Read before making a cloud in a jar.

title: Make a Cloud in a Bottle
desc: With warm water, ice on top and a little smoke from a match, the child makes a cloud form inside a glass jar in under 30 minutes.
how: An adult must handle the match.

title: Cloud in a Bottle
desc: Printable experiment that shows the three ingredients a cloud needs, moisture, tiny particles and cooling or a pressure change, by making one in a bottle.

title: Rain Gauge Activity
desc: Engineering challenge where the child designs and builds a tool from everyday materials to measure how much rain falls each day.
how: Perfect for the monsoon: keep a daily rainfall log for a few weeks.

title: Climate Kids: Weather vs Climate
desc: Illustrated page explaining that weather is what is happening outside now and changes quickly, while climate is the usual pattern of a place over about 30 years.

title: What's the Difference Between Weather and Climate? (video)
desc: Short NASA kids' video that explains how day-to-day weather differs from long-term climate.

title: What Can Trees Tell Us About Climate Change?
desc: Article showing how scientists read tree rings, along with ice cores and sediments, to learn about weather and climate hundreds or thousands of years ago.
how: Look for rings on a cut log or stump afterwards and count them together.

title: Make a Terrarium Mini-Garden
desc: The child builds a small garden in a clear glass jar with rocks, charcoal, soil and small plants, choosing plants with similar water needs, and watches water condense on the lid.
how: Links the greenhouse effect and the water cycle to something the child can watch every day.

title: Climate Kids: Make Something
desc: Collection of climate and Earth crafts and projects, such as a terrarium mini-garden and a lampshade garden that lets you see what's in the soil.

title: Climate Kids Printable Activities
desc: List of downloadable PDF versions of Climate Kids activities, including the terrarium mini-garden.

title: Climate Kids: Plants and Animals
desc: Articles on how satellites track plant health, what trees reveal about climate change and why NASA cares about food.

title: Power Savers
desc: Pledge and household tips: the child checks what is plugged in and switched on at home, unplugs idle chargers and turns off lights in empty rooms.
how: Make the child the family's 'power saver' for a week and keep a tally of switches turned off.

title: Go Green board game
desc: Printable board game that compares green and wasteful choices, such as reusing a water bottle instead of buying disposables, and shows how recycling keeps rubbish dumps from growing.

title: Trash and Climate Change activity books
desc: Printable children's activity books about how reusing and recycling things means factories make fewer new products, and how that helps the climate.

title: Learn About Landfills
desc: Children fill milk cartons with rubbish and soil, plant grass seed and watch what happens, and turn jugs and cartons into watering cans and seed pots.
how: Any tetra pack or plastic bottle works in place of milk cartons.

title: How Does a Rainbow Form?
desc: Short Indian article explaining how sunlight passing through raindrops makes the colours of a rainbow.
how: Read after spotting a monsoon rainbow, then make one with a garden hose with the Sun behind you.
